question.problem: Find the values of $\theta $ at which the curve $x=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,0\le \theta <2\pi $ intersects the line $x-y=0.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the coordinates of the points of intersection, we take the equation of the line, replace $x$ and $y$ with the parametric formulas, and then solve for $\theta .$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}x-y & =0 \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

The principal value of $\theta $ is

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$

This value lies inside the domain $0\le \theta <2\pi ,$ so our first solution is ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

To get a second solution, we add $\pi $ to ${\theta }_{1}:$

$$
{\theta }_{1}=\frac{\pi }{6}+\pi =\frac{7\pi }{6}
$$

Therefore, our solutions are $\frac{\pi }{6},\,\frac{7\pi }{6}.$
